prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not delay airway assessment in grade IV HE.
Avoid all benzodiazepines (alcohol withdrawal mgmt with phenobarbital or symptom-triggered low-dose if essential).
required_recommendations: Airway management — intubate if GCS <8 or inability to protect airway.
Lactulose enemas q4-6h; rifaximin via NG once airway secured.
Empiric IV thiamine 500 mg TID for 2-3 days before any dextrose.
Transplant evaluation triggered by recurrent severe HE.

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.
Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.

accepted: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade IV — coma), alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 24) — precipitated by binge alcohol relapse with medication non-adherence (lactulose/rifaximin not taken); ICU-level care with airway assessment indicated.

differential.key_features: Chronic alcoholic + binge + malnutrition; empiric thiamine before dextrose.
Grade IV obtundation warrants EEG to exclude NCSE.

key_clinical_evidence: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Grade IV HE = coma; airway protection is the immediate concern in addition to precipitant management.
Recurrent severe HE despite adherence should trigger transplant evaluation (AASLD).

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. K. is a 48-year-old man with severe alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 24) and a prior HE episode 3 months ago who was found unresponsive in his apartment by a neighbor. Emergency services report empty vodka bottles at the scene and the neighbor states the patient was found minimally responsive, unable to communicate. He had claimed sobriety since his outpatient detox 6 months ago. On arrival to the emergency department he has a GCS of 8 — eyes open only to pain, incomprehensible sounds, and localizing to pain. He is profoundly icteric with massive tense ascites and fetor hepaticus. Blood pressure is 108/66 with tachycardia 104. Serum ethanol is 182 mg/dL on admission. Ammonia is 212 µmol/L — the highest of his presentations. His lactulose and rifaximin were likely not taken during the binge.

neurological_exam.additional: Severe jaundice. Massive tense ascites — abdomen markedly distended. Multiple spider angiomata on chest and face. Caput medusae visible on abdomen. Fetor hepaticus strongly present. Palmar erythema. No fever. Paramedic states empty vodka bottles found at the apartment — estimated recent heavy binge drinking.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4 mm bilaterally, equal, reactive. Dolls eyes intact (brainstem preserved). Corneal reflexes present. No facial asymmetry. Gag reflex present but reduced.
neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 8 (E2V2M4). Minimally responsive to voice — opens eyes to painful stimulation only. Incomprehensible vocalizations. Localizes to pain in upper extremities. Cannot follow commands. Asterixis elicited with passive dorsiflexion — positive bilaterally. Profound disorientation.
neurological_exam.motor: Purposeful withdrawal upper extremities. Lower extremities withdraw to pain. Increased rigidity bilateral lower limbs.
neurological_exam.reflexes: DTRs 2+ upper, 1+ lower. Bilateral plantar responses: equivocal.
